Generated by haruspex from IR 0.21. Do not edit.
Each procedure's results are the schema in $defs under its name, and each named type is there too.
Every value is described as SQL Server's FOR JSON writes it, a rowset's rows as an array of objects.
The notes in descriptions rest on these facts:
- varchar(n) and char(n) count bytes, not characters. A character is one byte only in a single-byte collation, so elsewhere n bounds the length from above.
- JSON Schema counts a string's length in code points, and SQL Server in UTF-16 code units or bytes, of which a code point may take more than one, so a maximum length bounds the code points from above.

VariableAndTempOfOneNameRow.description: The type at results[0][] in lib.variable_and_temp_of_one_name.

variable_code.description: SQL type char(3). char(3) pads to 3 bytes and its collation isn't declared, so the length is 1 to 3 code points.

temp_code.description: SQL type varchar(10). varchar(10) counts bytes and its collation isn't declared, so the length is at most 10 code points. May be null: nullable-column (#tag.code).
